description.fun: A little electric mouse whose cheek sacs haven't finished growing, so it has to rub them furiously with its paw pads to make any electricity at all. Then it fires the charge from its forepaws, wobbling on its hind legs as it does. Even asleep it rubs its cheeks now and then, maybe practising. Its look draws on the alpine marmot, brought back to the Pyrenees in 1948.
description.guide: An Electric-type mouse Pokémon from Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, designed by Atsuko Nishida. Pawmi discharges electricity through the pads on its forepaws. It evolves into Pawmo and then Pawmot.
description.tagline: An electric mouse still learning to make sparks

description.fun: Pawmo travel in groups, and when theirs is attacked, Pawmo is the first to leap into the fight. Its signature technique strikes foes with its forepaws and zaps them through its paw pads at the same moment. It sometimes holds its battle stance even while asleep, perhaps dreaming of training.
description.guide: The middle stage of Pawmi's line, an Electric and Fighting-type Pokémon that fights by striking and shocking foes with its paw pads. It evolves into Pawmot after walking 1,000 steps with its Trainer outside its Poké Ball.
description.tagline: An electric mouse that punches and zaps at once

description.fun: Usually slow to react, Pawmot turns lightning-fast once a battle starts. Its fluffy fur works like a battery, storing as much electricity as an electric car. At heart it's peaceful, and it sometimes heals injured Pokémon with a jolt from its forepaws; if it raises its paws in its sleep, it may be dreaming of tending to others.
description.guide: The final evolution of Pawmi, an Electric and Fighting-type Pokémon whose fur stores electricity like a battery. It is slow to react outside battle but strikes with lightning speed in it.
description.tagline: A fluffy fighter with a battery for fur

transitions.how: Level up, after walking 1000 steps with it

note.text: Pawmo evolves only after walking 1,000 steps with its Trainer using the Let's Go! feature, outside its Poké Ball, then levelling up. The rule may nod to Ash's Pikachu, which never stays in its ball.
